# Pagination

Moves between numbered pages of a long list.

```tsx
import { Pagination } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- For lists that are split into pages, such as the blog or the programme archive.

## When not to

- For short lists: show them all.
- For endless feeds: use a "load more" button.

## Examples

### In-page paging

With `onPageChange` the items are buttons. The current page is `aria-current="page"`.

```tsx
<Demo />
```

### As links

With `hrefFor` the items are real links, so every page has its own address.

```tsx
<Pagination page={2} pageCount={6} hrefFor={(p) => `#pagina-${p}`} label="Páginas del blog" />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` (required) | `number` |  | Current page, starting at 1. |
| `pageCount` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` |  | Called with the new page. Use it for in-page paging (buttons). |
| `hrefFor` | `(page: number) => string` |  | Builds the URL of a page. When given, items are real links (`<a href>`): better for search engines and "open in a new tab". |
| `siblings` | `number` | `1` | Pages shown on each side of the current one. |
| `label` | `string` |  |  |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **Pattern:** `nav` labelled "Paginación" with the current page `aria-current="page"`.
- With `hrefFor` the items are real links, so pages are addressable and work without scripts; with `onPageChange` they are buttons.
- Previous and next say where they go; they are disabled at the ends.
- Every item is 44×44 px.

## Content

- Show at most seven items; the rest collapse into an ellipsis.
